doc.title: Lanny Morgan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999

chapter: Early road bands and the Army
title: Seventh Army Symphony and jazz band in Germany
summary: In Germany he played in the Army symphony and an 18-piece jazz band with Eddie Harris, Don Ellis and Cedar Walton.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: they call them in Germany, and then we had a jazz show, an 18-piece jazz band that did six months over there. And I couldn’t have been any more fortunate. Along with myself it was Eddie Harris and Leo Wright and Don Ellis and Cedar Walton. So it was really playing with good musicians and also the outside playing — we used to go to Heidelberg and play at The Cave, it was a jazz joint there. And then I played with the Symphony too, we did “Porgy and Bess” and another Gershwin thing. So it wasn’t time wasted, it was just dead time as far as what I really wanted.
Yeah you were off the scene.
Yeah, exactly. Why didn’t I think of that? You said it in three words.
